title: Combined Ratio and Percentage DI
tagline: Year 3 — Totals given with ratios: converting ratios to numbers and then to percentages, differences and combined ratios

introduction.overview: In many DI sets the data are given as totals and ratios rather than as direct numbers. The first step is to turn each ratio into actual values by splitting the total in the given ratio. After that you can compute percentages, differences and combined ratios. A particular trap is to add ratios directly (3 : 2 and 5 : 3 do not add to 8 : 5); you must convert to numbers first.
introduction.placementRelevance: Ratio-based DI sets are common in company and bank tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Gender ratios, budget splits and market shares are often published as ratios.

learningObjectives: Split a total in a given ratio
Combine ratios from different groups correctly

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: In a ratio a : b with total T, the first part is T × a ÷ (a + b) and the second is T × b ÷ (a + b).

coreDefinitions: Ratio: a comparison of two quantities by division.
Part: the share of the total for one term.
Combined ratio: ratio of totals, found from the actual numbers.
Common mistake: adding terms of ratios directly.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A ratio only tells you proportions. The total tells you the size. Together they fix the numbers.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For each row compute the first and second parts. Then build a table of actual numbers and work from it.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Combined
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Sum of parts ÷ sum of parts

mainNarrative: Class I has 300 students in the ratio 3 : 2, so boys = 300 × 3/5 = 180 and girls = 120. Class II: 400 in 5 : 3 gives boys 250 and girls 150. Class III: 350 in 4 : 3 gives boys 200 and girls 150. Class IV: 480 in 7 : 5 gives boys 280 and girls 200. Class V: 500 in 1 : 1 gives 250 each.
To avoid fractions, check divisibility before using a ratio on a total.
The combined ratio is found from the sums of the actual numbers, not from the given ratios.
Percentages come from the parts: boys in class I are 180 ÷ 300 = 60%.
Always verify that the parts add to the total.

deepDiveAspects.title: Adding ratios
deepDiveAspects.content: 3 : 2 and 5 : 3 combine into (3x + 5y) : (2x + 3y) depending on the totals; there is no fixed answer without numbers.

deepDiveAspects.title: Consistency of data
deepDiveAspects.content: Check that every part is whole before relying on a ratio.

solvedExamples.title: Split
solvedExamples.question: Class I has 300 students in the ratio boys : girls = 3 : 2. How many boys are there?

solvedExamples.title: Percent share
solvedExamples.question: In Class I there are 180 boys among 300 students. What percentage are boys?

solvedExamples.title: Combined ratio
solvedExamples.question: Class I has 180 boys and 120 girls; Class II has 250 boys and 150 girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls in the two classes together?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Convert every ratio into numbers once, then use a plain table.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the ratio as a percentage

placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Add boys and girls columns to the table.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I split a total in a ratio?
